text:
The air in the "Zen Garden" studio was thick with the scent of eucalyptus and the collective silence of twelve people attempting to achieve enlightenment. At the front of the room, Instructor Seraphina floated in a lotus position, her eyes closed, radiating an aura of serene perfection.

In the back row, Jim was having a very different experience.

Jim was a man who approached yoga with the same enthusiasm he usually reserved for assembling IKEA furniture without instructions. He had intended to join the "Gentle Stretching for Beginners" class, but due to a misread flyer and a profound misunderstanding of the word "Advanced," he had found himself in the room with the yogis who could apparently breathe through their ears.

The class began with "Mountain Pose." Jim stood up, wobbled, and immediately regretted his life choices. He looked around for guidance, but everyone else was already in a state of transcendent stillness. Jim decided to improvise. He lifted his arms, but instead of reaching for the sky, he flailed like a windmill in a hurricane.

"Namaste," Seraphina whispered, not opening her eyes.

Jim tried to mimic her. He bent forward, aiming for a standing forward fold. However, Jim’s center of gravity was located somewhere near his knees, and his flexibility was comparable to a rusted hinge. As he bent, his spine made a sound like a bag of chips being crushed. *Crunch.*

A few students in the front row twitched. Seraphina’s left eye opened a millimeter.

"Focus on your breath," Seraphina intoned.

Jim was trying to focus on not falling over. He shifted his weight to his left leg, but his right foot slipped on the mat. To compensate, he threw his arms out, knocking into the mat of the woman next to him, who was currently balancing on one hand in a complex variation of Crow Pose.

"Excuse me," Jim grunted, his face turning a shade of purple usually reserved for bruised plums.

He tried to recover by moving into "Downward Dog." This was a mistake. Jim did not look like a dog. He looked like a giraffe that had been stretched on a rack. His neck, which he had always considered a liability, was now the focal point of his awkwardness. He extended his arms and pushed his hips up, but his hamstrings were so tight they felt like steel cables.
